answer_1.quote: Question generation (QG) plays a crucial role ... we propose a novel framework named Chain-of-Exemplar (CoE), which combines retrieved exemplars and Chain-of-Thought (CoT) reasoning to generate educational questions and distractors from multimodal inputs of texts and images.
answer_1.outputs: Generated multiple-choice questions and plausible distractor answer options

answer_2.quote: Table presents the comparison of the automatic evaluation results of CoE with previous state-of-the-art models, which demonstrates that all the strong baselines fail to compete with CoE on both BLEU4 and ROUGE-L... We utilize Distinct-n scores as an automatic evaluation metric.

answer_4.quote: We randomly select 50 question samples generated by different methods and employ three annotators with good English background to rate them from 1 (worst) to 5 (best) based on 4 metrics: (1) Readability ... (2) Appropriateness ... (3) Complexity ... (4) Engagement ... We invited another three annotators to answer the selected 50 MCQs with the generated distractors ... and adopted a 5‑point scale for other 3 metrics: (1) Overlap ... (2) Plausibility ... (3) Distinctiveness.
answer_4.guideline: Annotators rate generated questions on Readability, Appropriateness, Complexity, and Engagement; for distractors they assess Overlap, Plausibility, Distinctiveness and answer accuracy.
